data.why: PTMVision's own bundled example sessions (loaded in-app via the Try Example buttons) already contain pre-computed UniProt annotations, AlphaFold structures and contact maps, so they are the reliable offline path to every exploration feature; the written CSV mirrors the app's own Plain/CSV template (bundled at app/ptmvision/static/resources/ptmvision.plain-format.template.csv) with pre-filled modification_unimod_id/mass_shift/classification columns (so no UniMod/UniProt lookup is needed to parse it) plus a missing-position row and an out-of-range position row to exercise the app's own error handling.

goals: Upload a PTM-containing search-engine result (or the Plain/CSV template) and get a unified, per-protein PTM table
Load a bundled example session (ionbot, Sage, MaxQuant, Spectronaut, MSFragger, mzIdentML, PeptideAtlas or Plain/CSV) to see a fully annotated dataset without preparing files
Explore the positions of PTMs along a protein's sequence and its predicted 3D structure
Check UniProt and UniMod annotations for a specific modified residue
Inspect which modified residues lie close to each other in 3D via the residue-residue contact map
Export the current analysis session and re-import it later to resume work

review.summary: The overview, protein-table and export parts are well structured, accurately labelled and well supported by the screens (two citations are weak). But the tree stops before the per-protein sequence, 3D structure, contact map and annotation views, which the README presents as PTMVision's main purpose. It needs a rerun where AlphaFold structures load, plus a real upload and a session re-import, before it captures what the tool is for.
